passages.title: Trees that cool city streets
passages.text: Many cities around the world are now planting trees along their streets. Scientists have found that trees can lower the temperature of a street by several degrees during hot summer days. This happens because leaves give shade and also release water into the air. Cooler streets mean that people use less electricity for air conditioning, which reduces costs for families. Trees also improve air quality, since they take in some of the pollution produced by cars. However, planting trees in a busy city is not simple. Roots can damage pipes under the road, and young trees need regular water for several years. Some cities have solved this problem by choosing species that grow deep roots and need little care. Local residents are often asked to help by watering the trees near their homes. Experts believe that these programs will become more important as summers grow hotter. For many urban planners, a street full of trees is no longer just attractive but necessary for public health.

main_ideas: Cities plant street trees because trees lower street temperatures.
Cooler streets save electricity and trees also clean the air.
